question.text: Per Reg 23, for unlisted securities where no MF Regulations valuation norm is prescribed, valuation shall follow guidelines endorsed by an AIF industry association whose membership represents at least what percentage of SEBI-registered AIFs?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per PDF Section 11.11: 'Valuation of securities, for which no valuation norm is prescribed under SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, shall be carried out as per valuation guidelines endorsed by any AIF industry association, which IN TERMS OF MEMBERSHIP REPRESENTS AT LEAST 33% OF THE NUMBER OF SEBI REGISTERED AIFs.' IVCA is the body that meets this threshold in India. The Trap: 10% / 25% / 51% are common distractors but none is the actual regulatory threshold. 33% is bright-line and directly ties to IVCA's qualification as the endorsing body. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same threshold. This is a detail-heavy regulatory question typical of SEBI inspections. Manager's Pro-Tip: If a new industry association emerges with 33%+ AIF membership and publishes alternative guidance, the AIF could in theory follow it. In practice, your LPs (especially DFIs and sovereigns) will demand IPEV/IVCA for consistency — document a clear rationale in the PPM.
